members.title: ‘Joy Bangla’ now a slogan for fleeing Awami League terrorists: Humaiun Kobir
members.lead: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir has said that ‘Joy Bangla’ has now become a slogan used by terrorists of the Awami League, whose activities are banned, as they flee. There will be no place for terrorists in Bangladesh. The state minister made the remarks while responding to questions from journalists at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Friday morning. A journalist asked whether the ongoing incidents of violence were damaging Bangladesh’s image internationally. In response, Humaiun Kobir said the Awami League has turned into a terrorist organisation. ‘Joy Bangla’ has now become a slogan used by Awami League terrorists as they fled. .Why the government is not cracking down on Awami League sabotage yet, and its strategy. No one would escape accountability for throwing petrol bombs or igniting fires, while shouting ‘Joy Bangla’ and then running away. Such activities would be dealt with through strict enforcement of the law, he added. The state minister said the Awami League’s activities were currently suspended because of its involvement in terrorist activities. The party has now been reduced to carrying out isolated acts of terrorism. Its activities appeared to consist of throwing petrol bombs or setting fires in different places before fleeing. . Referring to Awami League leaders living abroad, Humaiun Kobir said law enforcement agencies were working on the matter of their activities. No one would escape justice, and they would eventually be brought under the law. . People in the country would not be intimidated by such acts of terrorism. Nor would petrol bomb attacks or any other means create an opportunity to bring the party’s fugitive terrorists back to Bangladesh from abroad, he added. . members.title: Jaiswal declines to comment on Bangladesh’s internal affairs
members.lead: Randhir Jaiswal, spokesperson for India’s Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), declined to make any comment on Bangladesh’s internal affairs. Speaking at a press briefing at the MEA in New Delhi today, Friday, Jaiswal refrained from responding to questions regarding recent protests and violence carried out by leaders and activists of the Awami League, whose activities are banned in Bangladesh, across various districts of the country, as well as Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s remarks on the issue—stating simply that he had nothing to say on Bangladesh’s internal developments. However, Jaiswal noted that India’s position regarding its relationship with the neighbouring country remains unchanged. India has consistently expressed its desire to foster a positive, constructive, and forward-looking relationship with Bangladesh—one anchored in shared history, cultural ties, and people-to-people connections. . Sheikh Hasina, who fled to India following her ouster in the July Mass Uprising, has announced her intention to return to Bangladesh in December. Following programme announcements on social media by the Awami League, incidents of sabotage—including arson attacks on buses and the hurling of crude bombs—have been occurring across several districts, including Gopalganj. Speaking about this at a public rally in Lalmonirhat yesterday, Thursday, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman stated that the people of the country no longer wish to return to the politics of enforced disappearances, killings, arson terrorism, and the deprivation of voting rights. .PM directs MPs to remain on the ground to tackle sabotage by Awami League. Criticising Awami League leaders without naming the party directly, the prime minister remarked that they never cared for the interests of this country or its people, adding that the country across the border to which they fled is their “master,” and that they have resumed conspiring against the people of Bangladesh to appease those masters.
